name: Leggy Flow — Dead Clean → Curtsy → Lateral Lunge → Lateral Squat Clean → Tactical Clean
description: A leggy single-bell kettlebell flow from a Madeleine Conti reel — the lower-body cousin of the Bent Press Flow (kb-flow-dead-clean-press). Same dead-clean entry and tactical-clean exit, but the middle is all lunge / lateral-squat work instead of front squat + bent press. Dead clean from the floor, curtsy lunge in the rack, lateral lunge swinging the bell back, clean up into a lateral squat, lateral lunge again, then step the feet together for a tactical clean. Run the full sequence on one side, then the other. No overhead pressing — friendly on the right shoulder.
flowNotes: **This is a continuous FLOW, not separate stations.** Move through the whole chain on ONE side — dead clean → curtsy lunge → lateral lunge → lateral squat clean → lateral lunge → tactical clean — letting each move feed the next, then repeat on the other side. Single MEDIUM bell (~25-35lb); quality and continuity over load. The cleans come from the legs and hips, not the arm. 3 rounds each side.

flowSequence.notes: Dead stop on the floor, explosive pull to the rack — soft knees to catch, zero impact.
Bell stays racked. Step the trailing leg back and across, knee toward the floor, torso tall, front knee tracks the toes.
Swing the bell DOWN between the legs as you step wide — hips back, trailing leg straight. The swing-back loads the next move.
From the bottom, drive out of the lateral lunge and clean the bell to the rack as you come up into a lateral squat. Leg + hip power makes the clean — the arm just guides. Catch soft.
Swing the bell back down between the legs again — second lateral lunge, controlled.
Smooth, controlled return to the rack — closes the flow before switching sides.

tips: This is a FLOW — the six moves connect seamlessly, no pausing between them. Smooth, controlled transitions are the point.
Single MEDIUM bell — movement quality and continuity over load. The cleans and the lateral squat clean are powered by the legs and hips, not the arm.
Run the full sequence on one side, then the other. 3 rounds each side is a solid dose; for a conditioning version, run 2-3 rounds/side as one set, rest 1 min, repeat for 4-5 sets.
Curtsy lunge stays racked; the lateral lunges swing the bell down between the legs to load the next clean.
No overhead pressing in this flow — friendly on the right shoulder. The highest the bell goes is the rack.
Great for hip mobility, adductor strength, lateral-plane power, and full-body coordination.
